facts.text: Southwest is an unincorporated community in Westmoreland County, Pennsylvania, located just off Pennsylvania Route 981.
The Westmoreland County Historical Society, founded in 1908, preserves the county’s rich industrial and ethnic heritage.
The Allegheny‑Kiski Valley Historical Society interprets the cultural history of southwestern Pennsylvania, including the area around Southwest.
Washington County, just south of Southwest, is home to 23 historic covered bridges, the second most of any county in Pennsylvania.
Southwest’s landscape blends rolling country hills with the conveniences of nearby city life, a mix highlighted by local tourism guides.
The region’s history is celebrated through museums and historic sites that trace the development of southwestern Pennsylvania.
